result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers correctly say that Georgia's old-style figures and left alignment cause the wandering numbers, and both give similar, correct CSS plus advice to format decimals consistently. B sets the header apart in more concrete ways: weight, a smaller size, a muted color and a heavier rule underneath. It also explains the reasoning a bit more fully, for example how the place-value columns line up. B does add some extras, like styling the ID column, an nth-child alternative and an option that rounds 611.25 to 611.3. A is tighter and easier to act on. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers find the same main problems: left-aligned numbers, Georgia's old-style figures, uneven decimals and headers that blend into the data. Both also give similar CSS that right-aligns the number columns and uses tabular figures. A sets the header apart more clearly, but it adds extra suggestions and its default of 1 decimal for weight would round 611.25 to 611.3 and lose precision. B is tighter, keeps every value by using 2 decimals, and stays proportionate, though its header fix is only a weight change.
